# driver

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/internal/driver"
```

Package driver owns a module compilation and its generated files.

The driver decides which files to compile and when to publish the result. The [frontend](<https://github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/blob/main/internal/frontend/readme.md>), [checker](<https://github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/blob/main/internal/checker/readme.md>), and [lowering](<https://github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/blob/main/internal/lowering/readme.md>) packages handle syntax, types, and Go code. They do not decide which files the driver can replace.

### Source and build selection

TGo input controls each output. For example, service\_linux\_test.tgo produces service\_tgo\_linux\_test.go. Compilation starts at the module root. It keeps dependencies, assets, and module replacements at their original paths so that Go selects the same build inputs as a normal build.

Go tools select files by Go filenames. The driver therefore puts TGo source at its generated paths before it requests build metadata. Go selects platform files, build tags, and test packages. Nested modules and dependency directories remain outside the driver's output ownership.

### Stage results and output ownership

Reading returns an ordered source list. Selection returns Go build metadata. Checking returns typed packages and selected output paths. Lowering returns replacement contents and excluded paths. Each stage receives its input explicitly. Lowering builds the output before publication writes it.

Compile owns rollback from the first source copy through the final Go check. Failure restores old generated bytes and permissions and removes new outputs. Success keeps the new Go files and removes excluded outputs. Go module metadata changes remain in either case.

## func Compile

```go
func Compile(dir string)
```

Compile translates the module's TGo files into Go files in the same module. On failure, it restores previous generated files and panics.
